inspected_anchors.finding: Identity and abstract.
Reference entailment oracle and exchangeable complete examples.
Sound back-off and strictly safe threshold; lower guarantee need not require nested sets.
Theorem4.1: exchangeability, soundness, distinct scores and alpha>=1/(n+1); nesting additionally for upper bound.
Merger assumption is semantic equivalence, not probabilistic independence.
Subclaim shortcut; partial-entailment notation needs separate inspection before implementation.
Base/splitter/merger and score roles.
50 first inputs per dataset, author labels, tie rules and resampling.
1000 repeated half-splits; fixed calibration variation and marginal scope.
Explicit domain/user/fixed-calibration/distribution-shift limitations.

supported_claims: Entailment-oracle-relative lower validity uses safe back-off thresholds without universal nesting; tight upper bound has extra nesting condition.
Merger entailment equivalence does not assume statistical independence of claims.
Published finite order-statistic range is alpha>=1/(n+1).
Small author-annotated samples and repeated splits do not create new independent evidence; marginal validity excludes per-input and shifted guarantees.
limitations: Author primary-text review, not independent review or empirical reproduction.
No new pixel review; six-image allowance exhausted. Pseudocode has alternate text extraction.
No downloaded code or live model executed. Underlying papers, repositories and model claims need separate originals before new technical reliance.
Public/authored benchmarks do not establish bank truth, identification, native capability, deployment prevalence or ROI.
Claim-dependency graph is not intervention DAG; inspection does not endorse every claim or close coverage.

inspected_anchors.finding: Identity; printed/archive dates distinct.
Splitter/reference assumptions and exchangeability/ties.
Contextual deducibility; relevance not guaranteed.
Superstring assumption; oracle ideal graphs.
Semantic approximate-graph properties; practical validity cannot be enforced rigorously.
Post-hoc versus subgraph filtering.
Actual safe-subgraph score and strict threshold selection.
Lower bound independent of graph quality; upper adds semantic graph and finite bad threshold.
Gold subset versus silver graph-assisted labels; FELM silver only.
Miscalibration, task dependence, legibility surrogate and retention findings.
Re-prompt results separate; long graphs and subjective truth limits.
Ideal graph proof inspected but not independently verified wholesale.
Forward lower-bound argument uses actual subset truth, not graph quality.
Reverse upper-bound direction invokes semantic graph and nesting; FELM limits.

supported_claims: Lower coherent-factuality bound can use actual subset truth without perfect proxy graphs; tight upper bound adds semantic graph and finite-threshold conditions.
Silver label shortcut relies on graph assumptions; direct gold subset labels are distinct.
FELM miscalibration, cyclic/long-output problems and subjective rubric limit generalization.
Regenerated outputs are a separately evaluated outcome, not automatically certified.
limitations: Author primary-text review, not independent review or empirical reproduction.
No new pixel review; six-image allowance exhausted. Pseudocode has alternate text extraction.
No downloaded code or live model executed. Underlying papers, repositories and model claims need separate originals before new technical reliance.
